title: Release Lighthouse: synchronized cut criteria and release notes playbook for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Summary:
This ticket creates a canonical cross-team playbook (Release Lighthouse) to coordinate milestone cadence, scope-lock rules, and cut criteria for the API, Console, and Runtime release train. The playbook is intended to reduce ambiguity during the last 4 weeks of the cycle, unify release-note generation, and create deterministic rollback criteria that can be executed by engineering, product, and design.

Goals: 
- Define a single source of truth for scope freeze and cutline decisions across API, Console, and Runtime.
- Provide a templated release-notes workflow with owners for feature highlights, breaking changes, and migration guides.
- Specify cut criteria (quality, perf, infra, docs) and the operational steps for partial/feature cut or full rollback.
- Create lightweight automation hooks (GitHub label -> release bucket, Confluence release notes section) to speed authoring.

Scope: 
In scope: milestone calendar, triage protocol, per-component cut criteria, release notes ownership matrix, preflight checklist, emergency rollback play.
Out of scope: marketing comms copywriting, post-launch sales enablement assets (handled by GTM team), deep platform reliability upgrades (handled by separate SRE epic).

Milestones (proposed):
- M1 (T-28): Feature owners declared, owners in release-notes doc assigned, initial canary testing plan in runtime-sandbox written.
- M2 (T-18): Integration smoke tests passing across API/Console/Runtime; docs draft complete; release notes skeleton published.
- M3 (T-10): Scope lock enforced (only P0 bugfixes), all shipping PRs merged and flagged with release label.
- M4 (T-3): Final release notes freeze and sign-off; release candidates cut.
- M5 (T+1): Post-launch telemetry check and rollback decision window closed.

Cut Criteria (per-component summary):
- API: No 95th+ latency regression >15% on measured golden suite; no new 5xxs in staging for 24h; documented API contract changes reviewed by SDK owners.
- Console: No blocking UI regressions on critical flows (login, deployments, rollouts); automated end-to-end smoke green; accessibility audit passed for new controls.
- Runtime: Kernel/quantization changes must show no >10% p99 latency increase on representative workload; autoscaler behavior validated under synthetic load; KV cache correctness verified.

Decision ladder: 
- If any P0 fails for a component, attempt patch -> canary -> partial routing to fallback model variant. If failure cannot be mitigated within T-6, escalate to release board and apply scoped cut (component-level cut) rather than full train rollback unless multiple components are impacted.

Release Notes Workflow: 
- Owners: feature owners add one-paragraph summary + customer value + migration notes in Confluence template under Release Lighthouse page.
- PR linkage: GitHub PRs must include a release-notes section and apply label "rls:2025.07". A small utility script will aggregate labeled PR descriptions into the release draft.
- Responsible approver: PM lead (assignee) and Design reviewer will sign off on language and screenshots. Engineering will verify technical accuracy.

Operational runbook artifacts (links):
- Release Lighthouse Confluence (draft): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Release+Lighthouse+2025.07
- Release notes draft (auto-aggregate): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/release-lighthouse-2025-07
- Canary perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rls/canary-2025-07
- GitHub label query: https://github.com/redwood-inference/issues/labels/rls-2025-07

Acceptance criteria: 
- Release playbook page with owner matrix published and acknowledged by Eng, Design, and PM leads.
- Automation script can collect labeled PR entries into a single draft.
- Cut criteria test checklist created and used in the T-10 smoke run.
- Rollback decision tree rehearsed once in a tabletop exercise.

Success metrics (post-launch window):
- Less than 2 unplanned hotfix PRs post T+7 for cross-component regressions.
- Release-note draft completed 72 hours before cut with sign-offs.
- Canary to production rollout latency under target SLO for >90% requests during ramp.

Open risks & trade-offs: 
- Trade-off: Strict scope lock reduces feature churn but delays smaller UX polish items; recommended: "two-week grace" sandbox for low-risk cosmetic changes.
- Risk: Automation aggregation depends on consistent PR hygiene; mitigation: educate teams + small GitHub action to warn on missing release sections.
- Risk: Per-component owners unfamiliar with cut criteria; mitigation: we will run a 60-minute workshop two cycles before adoption.

Next steps: 
1) Finalize playbook wording and ratify by component leads (target 2025-06-20).
2) Ship GitHub action for release-note label enforcement (ENG-24418).
3) Schedule tabletop rollback rehearsal (invite list: eng-sre, runtime, api, console, legal).
4) Publish public-facing release notes template and sample.

Notes: This ticket aims to be the operational spine for all cross-component trains; keep it lightweight and iteratively improve after two releases.
